appended_meaning:
The current State/local trafficking law-enforcement grant program is another qualified authority component of the same CJS trafficking line, not a separate member vote or whole-line allocation. Complete pre-vote 34 USC 20705 maps to original 2005 section 204, formerly 42 USC 14044c. Complete original section 204 and 2013 section 1242 preserve the actual citizenship/permanent-residence condition and its express deletion; that old condition is not a current recipient or offense limitation. The territorial-jurisdiction requirement remains: the described severe-trafficking acts and related offenses occur wholly or partly within the United States. Related offenses include tax, illegal-proceeds, money-laundering, racketeering and other criminal violations committed in connection with sex trafficking or a severe form of trafficking. This is not every unrelated tax or financial offense, every offense worldwide or an individual immigration/criminal classification.

The Attorney General may make grants to States and local law-enforcement agencies for the complete listed program purposes: investigation/prosecution, victim-identification training, purchaser investigations/prosecutions prioritizing minor-victim cases, education of persons charged with or convicted of purchasing or attempting to purchase commercial sex, trust/cooperation training, and as appropriate designation of at least one severe-trafficking prosecutor. These are qualified grant purposes, not a new criminal offense, actual prosecution, universal prosecutor appointment, automatic award or proof that every grantee performs every purpose. The purchaser-case priority does not restrict all grant purposes to child cases. The printed severe-trafficking reference to 7102(9) retains its explicit original note tracing redesignation to current 7102(11); existing complete current definitions are reused without silent reference repair or a separate individual victim determination.

Grants may be made only for programs where the State/local law-enforcement agency collaborates with social-service providers and relevant nongovernmental organizations, including organizations experienced in services to trafficked persons. That mandatory program collaboration is distinct from training officers to encourage a person's cooperation with prosecution. It does not itself require every victim to collaborate with police, turn the nonexclusive experienced-organization example into the only possible partner, or import the separate 20702/20703 service-access assurances as new 20705 text. The current Federal share cannot exceed 75 percent of the total costs of projects described in the application. This is a Federal project-cost ceiling, not a minimum, a percent of the entire $88 million, the other program's grant match or the child program's year-based Federal shares. Existing qualified CJS transfer, research/evaluation and notification rules remain separately bound; no automatic combined deduction, invented program administration cap or net award is calculated.

An entity applying for a 20702 grant is not prohibited from also applying here; current 20702 separately preserves the reciprocal savings. Concurrent applications do not guarantee eligibility, awards, double funding or both programs' conditions being interchangeable. Current authorization is $10 million for each fiscal year 2014-2021, distinct from original 2005 $25 million for fiscal years 2006-2007 and the 2013 amendment's then-2014-2017 range. Those dated authorization objects are not new H.R. 1968 appropriations, observed grants or automatic termination of the program. The GAO study/report duty within thirty months after March 7, 2013 and its specified evaluation/recommendation scope remains dated, without claiming the report occurred or imposing a new current deadline.

This completes the bounded current 20705 program and identified original/current mapping, not all trafficking-fund applications or the whole package. Material fund-use/medical-transfer conditions and exact 2101(d)-(e), further center authorities where applied, State/migration/refugee assistance, supplementary acts, other DHS, exact counterparts and final package comparison remain executable research. No new application question, individual status/benefit/provider/criminal disposition, separate member stance or editorial acceptance is inferred.

operative_witnesses.passage: (a) Establishment of grant program for law enforcement (1) In general The Attorney General may make grants to States and local law enforcement agencies to establish, develop, expand, or strengthen programs— (A) to investigate and prosecute acts of severe forms of trafficking in persons, and related offenses that occur, in whole or in part, within the territorial jurisdiction of the United States; (B) to train law enforcement personnel how to identify victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons and related offenses; (C) to investigate and prosecute persons who engage in the purchase of commercial sex acts and prioritize the investigations and prosecutions of those cases involving minor victims; (D) to educate persons charged with, or convicted of, purchasing or attempting to purchase commercial sex acts; (E) to educate and train law enforcement personnel in how to establish trust of persons subjected to trafficking and encourage cooperation with prosecution efforts; and (F) as appropriate, to designate at least 1 prosecutor for cases of severe forms of trafficking in persons (as such term is defined in section 7102(9) 1 of title 22). (2) Definition In this subsection, the term "related offenses" includes violations of tax laws, transacting in illegally derived proceeds, money laundering, racketeering, and other violations of criminal laws committed in connection with an act of sex trafficking or a severe form of trafficking in persons. (b) Multi-disciplinary approach required Grants under subsection (a) may be made only for programs in which the State or local law enforcement agency works collaboratively with social service providers and relevant nongovernmental organizations, including organizations with experience in the delivery of services to persons who are the subject of trafficking in persons. (c) Limitation on Federal share The Federal share of a grant made under this section may not exceed 75 percent of the total costs of the projects described in the application submitted. (d) No limitation on section 20702 grant applications An entity that applies for a grant under section 20702 of this title is not prohibited from also applying for a grant under this section. (e) Authorization of appropriations There are authorized to be appropriated to the Attorney General to carry out this section $10,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2014 through 2021. (f) GAO evaluation and report Not later than 30 months after March 7, 2013, the Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a study of and submit to Congress a report evaluating the impact of this section on— (1) the ability of law enforcement personnel to identify victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons and investigate and prosecute cases against offenders, including offenders who engage in the purchasing of commercial sex acts with a minor; and (2) recommendations, if any, regarding any legislative or administrative action the Comptroller General determines appropriate to improve the ability described in paragraph (1).
